messages:
maria.ortiz: Hey team — ACME's vendor risk just asked for our incident disclosure windows and exact timelines for a 30d hosted POC. They want committed ack + preliminary + final report timelines. Can we confirm what we state for POC vs Dedicated vs Private?

kevin_ng: For POCs (hosted) our typical guidance is: acknowledge within 24h, preliminary findings within 72h, full forensics & mitigation plan within 14 days. Dedicated customers can often get 8h ack and a 7-day full report if contracted. Private (VPC/on-prem) is customer-run; we provide the runbook and support cadence but timelines are negotiated.

samir_ch: Quick note on regulatory: if confirmed data exfiltration triggers GDPR/other regs, customers usually handle regulator notification. We provide the incident package to enable filings. We should avoid promising to file on behalf of customers unless legal signs off in the SOW. Also severity affects timelines — severe incidents escalate faster.

maria.ortiz: Sales needs copy for contracts and a short email template for POC. Also buyer asked if we do '72h ack' vs '72h update' — they want precise phrasing.

janelle_lee: Legal: prefer we separate 'acknowledgment' from 'notification'. We can commit to 'acknowledge within X hours' and 'deliver a preliminary impact assessment within Y hours/days' and 'final technical report within Z days'. For hosted POCs use conservative defaults (24h/72h/14d). I'll draft contract language that clarifies customer responsibility for regulator notices unless otherwise agreed.

kevin_ng: Logistics summary for sales: hosted POC = 24h ack / 72h preliminary / 14d full report. Dedicated (enterprise) = negotiable, example 8h ack / 48–72h preliminary / 7d full report. Private = per-customer runbook + on-call handoff. Also call out that 'preliminary' may be a high-level impact statement if forensic work is ongoing.

samir_ch: Operational detail: If we see confirmed exfiltration or active compromise, internal escalation lane triggers IR pager -> IR lead within 1 hour. For POC customers we still run the IR playbook internally; external comms follow the windows above unless the customer requests immediate notification.

maria.ortiz: Can someone paste a short customer-facing initial acknowledgment template I can use for ACME?

kevin_ng: ```Hi <Customer>, thanks for flagging this to us. We have received your report and opened an incident (INC-2001xxx). Our security team has triaged and will provide a preliminary update within 72 hours. If the incident is classified as high-severity, a dedicated incident lead will be assigned and you'll receive an update within 24 hours. We will deliver a final technical incident report within fourteen (14) days, subject to reasonable extensions for forensic activities. Regards, Kevin (Solutions)```

janelle_lee: Slight legal tweak: replace 'we will deliver' with 'we will provide to the POC contact' and add a confidentiality sentence. Also add: "Customer is responsible for regulatory filings unless otherwise agreed in writing."

samir_ch: FYI the buyer also asked for our CAIQ/SIG baseline. For POC we can share a redacted CAIQ export. I'll upload a sanitized file to the secure share and send the link.

maria.ortiz: Another ACME Q: do you notify affected tenants automatically or only if impacted data is confirmed?

samir_ch: Hosted: we notify impacted tenants/customers only if we confirm their data or tenant was impacted. We will include an affected-tenant list in the incident report. Dedicated/private: notification approach is controlled by the customer and defined in the runbook/contract.

kevin_ng: Sales one-liner to use: "Redwood will acknowledge security reports within 24 hours for hosted POCs, provide a preliminary impact assessment within 72 hours, and deliver a full technical incident report within fourteen (14) days; enterprise customers may negotiate accelerated SLAs."

maria.ortiz: Perfect — I'll send to ACME now. @janelle_lee can you drop the contract clause? @samir_ch can you attach the sanitized CAIQ link?

janelle_lee: Draft clause below: ```Security Incident Notification: Upon receipt of a security report, Redwood will acknowledge receipt within twenty-four (24) hours and provide a preliminary impact assessment within seventy-two (72) hours. Redwood will provide a final technical incident report within fourteen (14) calendar days, subject to reasonable extension for forensic activities. Customer is responsible for regulatory filings and external notifications unless otherwise agreed in writing.```

samir_ch: Uploaded redacted CAIQ here: https://redwood-secureshare/caqi/acme_poc_redacted.pdf :thumbsup:

maria.ortiz: Thanks all — sending now. :raised_hands:
